newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says may cancel futures bourse licence.
newsitem.headline: Manila says may cancel futures bourse licence.

text.p: The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Thursday it was considering cancellation of the licence of the Manila International Futures Exchange (MIFE).
"There is a strong possibility that there will be a final revocation of their (MIFE'S) licence and we will act on it in a few day's time," SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay told reporters.
Yasay said the head of the management committee hired by MIFE to implement a range of reforms had resigned.
"The (proposed) reforms submitted were cosmetic and would have rendered the new management committee unable to institute substantial changes," he said.
The SEC will no longer require MIFE to submit new reform proposals, Yasay said.
The SEC suspended MIFE operations on June 20, 1996 due to complaints from the public of widespread irregularities.
The exchange had offered contracts in copra, sugar, dry cocoon, soybeans, coffee and major currencies but dealers said its trading volumes were very low. The exchange had less than 10 brokers.
MIFE officials were not immediately available for comment.
